Mental Health Screening & Evaluation Resource
 Packet
This informational packet outlines common standardized screening tools used by professionals to help
identify symptoms of psychological disorders. Please note: Screening tools are intended to guide
conversations with a healthcare provider and do not replace a formal clinical diagnosis.
1. Common Screening Tools & Public Availability
Many foundational rating scales are in the public domain and widely accessible to the public, while
other proprietary diagnostic tools require a clinician license to purchase and administer.

2. Sample Self-Screening Tool: GAD-7 (Anxiety)
Instruction: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following problems? (0 =
Not at all, 1 = Several days, 2 = More than half the days, 3 = Nearly every day)
1. Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge [ 0 ] [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ]
2. Not being able to stop or control worrying [ 0 ] [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ]
3. Worrying too much about different things [ 0 ] [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ]
4. Trouble relaxing [ 0 ] [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ]
5. Being so restless that it is hard to sit still [ 0 ] [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ]
6. Becoming easily annoyed or irritable [ 0 ] [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ]
7. Feeling afraid, as if something awful might happen [ 0 ] [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ]

3. Next Steps for Professional Evaluation
 Consult a Primary Care Provider: Your doctor can perform routine blood work to rule out
physical health conditions (like thyroid issues) that mimic mental health symptoms.
 Connect with a Specialist: Seek out a licensed clinic
